# sysutils_file (Data Source)

Reads an existing regular file's contents, checksums, size, mode, ownership and modification time without managing it. Use it to feed the contents of a host file into other resources, to react to changes of a file maintained by something else, or to copy a file's ownership.

Unlike the [`sysutils_directory`](./directory.md) data source, a missing file **is** an error, because the contents cannot be null. A directory, FIFO, socket or device at `path` is an error too.

A symlink at `path` is refused unless `follow_symlinks = true` is set. This matches the [security model](../index.md#security-model) of the resources: reading through a symlink that another user can plant or redirect (for example in `/tmp`) could expose the contents of a file that user cannot read into Terraform state and outputs.

The data source is read during planning, so it sees the filesystem as it is before the apply. Files that resources in the same configuration will create are not visible until the next run.

## Example Usage

### Read a text file

```terraform
data "sysutils_file" "machine_id" {
  path = "/etc/machine-id"
}

output "machine_id" {
  value = trimspace(data.sysutils_file.machine_id.content)
}
```

### Follow a symlink explicitly

```terraform
# /etc/os-release is usually a symlink to /usr/lib/os-release.
data "sysutils_file" "os_release" {
  path            = "/etc/os-release"
  follow_symlinks = true
}
```

### Copy a binary file and restart a service when another file changes

```terraform
data "sysutils_file" "ca_cert" {
  path = "/etc/ssl/private/ca.der"
}

resource "sysutils_file" "ca_copy" {
  path           = "/opt/app/ca.der"
  content_base64 = data.sysutils_file.ca_cert.content_base64
  mode           = data.sysutils_file.ca_cert.mode
  owner          = data.sysutils_file.ca_cert.owner
  group          = data.sysutils_file.ca_cert.group
}

resource "sysutils_exec" "reload" {
  command = ["systemctl", "restart", "app"]
  triggers = {
    ca = data.sysutils_file.ca_cert.content_sha256
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `path` (String) Absolute path of the file to read. Must be in canonical form (no `.`/`..` segments, duplicate or trailing slashes) and must not be `/`.

### Optional

- `follow_symlinks` (Boolean) If `true` and `path` is a symlink, read the file it points to; all attributes then describe the target, not the link. Defaults to `false`, in which case a symlink at `path` is an error. If the provider's `root_dir` is set, the link is resolved inside it: absolute targets are relative to `root_dir`, and a link leading above `root_dir` is an error.

### Read-Only

- `content` (String) File contents as text. Null if the file is not valid UTF-8; use `content_base64` for binary files.
- `content_base64` (String) File contents as standard (padded) base64. Always set, also for text files.
- `content_md5` (String) Hex-encoded MD5 checksum of the file contents. Provided for interoperability; use `content_sha256` where integrity matters.
- `content_sha256` (String) Hex-encoded SHA-256 checksum of the file contents.
- `gid` (Number) Numeric GID of the group.
- `group` (String) Group name, or the numeric GID as a string if it has no group entry.
- `id` (String) Data source identifier (equal to `path`).
- `mode` (String) Four-digit octal mode of the file, including setuid, setgid and sticky bits (e.g. `"0644"`, `"4755"`).
- `modified` (String) Last modification time in [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) format, in UTC with second precision (e.g. `"2024-02-29T11:34:56Z"`).
- `owner` (String) Username of the owner, or the numeric UID as a string if it has no passwd entry.
- `size` (Number) Size of the contents in bytes.
- `uid` (Number) Numeric UID of the owner.

## Errors

| Situation | Diagnostic |
|-----------|------------|
| Nothing exists at `path` (or a parent directory is missing) | `File not found` |
| `path` is a symlink and `follow_symlinks` is not `true` | `Symbolic link refused` |
| `path` is a symlink whose target does not exist, with `follow_symlinks = true` | `File not found` |
| `path` is a directory (or, with `follow_symlinks = true`, a symlink to one) | `Is a directory` |
| `path` is a FIFO, socket or device | `Not a regular file` |
| The file is not readable by the user running Terraform | `Open failed` |

## Caveats

- The file's contents are stored in Terraform state, in `content_base64` and, for text files, also in `content`. Do not read secrets unless your state backend is encrypted and access-controlled.
- The whole file is read into memory, and stored twice for text files. Point the data source only at reasonably small files; to react to changes of a large file, prefer a [`sysutils_file`](../resources/file.md) resource with `source`, which streams the contents.
- The file is opened once, non-blocking (so a FIFO swapped in cannot hang the provider), and every attribute is taken from that open descriptor. Contents and metadata therefore always describe the same file, even if `path` is replaced concurrently. `size` is the number of bytes actually read.
- Symlinks in the *parent* components of `path` are always followed, as for the resources.
- The data source only works on Unix-like systems.
